column16: I believe it's a bit harder to punch the incoming balls in the right direction.

We encountered quite a few odd interactions with the colliders of the ball, the "hands" and the head of the player avatar. I do believe the application is still under refinement, but it did feel that testing those odd interactions felt a lot more interesting than the core gameplay, for playing it as a focused wasn't too interesting for me.
column22: My preferred setting would be somewhere between level 1 and 2, in terms of the auditory response, but 2 on the visual density. Despite that, I chose 1 simply because of the reactions of the crowd. I'm not aware of the implementation part of it, but because there was only a general background track playing for the audience at different modes, it was just hard to focus when the density was too high, even after making volume adjustments. As such, level 1 seemed the most tame as it had realistic enough energy for a crowd that size, while not being okay with the audio.
